conceptZh: 戴獵鹿帽的豬探長發現地上一排泥腳印，拿放大鏡一路跟蹤繞了一圈，越跟越興奮——最後停下來低頭一看，腳印正好接到自己的鞋子上，他整個僵住。
object: a stout cartoon detective pig in a deerstalker hat with a magnifying glass, and a trail of muddy hoofprints
morph: the glyph 豬 stands still as a solid sculpture while the detective follows the hoofprints in a loop in front of it
creativeAngle: 孩子喜歡的豬探長主角再次登場，但笑點和日那支完全不同：這次是「跟蹤腳印跟回自己身上」的推理笑話，動作路線繞一圈也讓畫面有節奏。豬左豕右者共十五畫，靠字體靜止保結構。語音詞「山豬」，山ㄕㄢ剛學過，兩字都只有一種讀音，也避開和小那支重複的小豬。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 豬 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated rich burgundy, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 豕 radical on the left and the 者 component on the right stay clearly separated, with the dot above 者 and all of its horizontal strokes evenly spaced. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. In front of its base, a stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat and a tiny trench coat spots a line of muddy hoofprints on the ground. From 0.6 seconds he drops into a crouch, magnifying glass out, and follows them with mounting excitement: left along the bottom of frame, up the right side, back across, tracking faster and faster, tail wagging harder the closer he gets. At 3.2 seconds the trail curves sharply and he skids to a stop, leaning right down to the very last print. He looks at the print. He looks at his own muddy shoe sitting exactly on top of it. He looks at the print again. At 4.0 seconds he goes completely still, ears drooping, then quietly tucks the magnifying glass into his coat and tiptoes out of frame to the left, taking the hoofprints with him as they fade away behind him by 4.7 seconds. From 4.8 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 豬 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「豬、豬、山豬」, using the reading ㄓㄨ for 豬 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 豬 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 山豬 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 豬: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 機器人想摸摸小豬，長手卻把彈性小豬壓成扁餅；小豬彈回原形，反把機器人的長手送到自己頭上。
object: An eager boxy toy robot assembled from mismatched parts, with one noticeably longer arm, and one pink rubber pig with a round snout and curly tail.
morph: The complete glyph remains stationary and intact while a rubber pig compresses and rebounds beside it, demonstrating the character’s meaning through physical comedy.
creativeAngle: 改用不對稱長短手的機器人與彈性小豬，取代追查腳印。長手摸豬失手變成摸自己，最後靠近一步、改用短手成功；字形全程固定，避免笑點干擾筆畫辨識。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked-off wide shot. Against a light buttercream background, place the single Traditional Chinese glyph 豬 precisely at frame center, uncropped, occupying approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Render it in saturated burgundy using a verified standard Taiwanese Traditional Chinese textbook glyph, with the complete 豕 component on the left and 者 on the right. Preserve every stroke, gap and proportion throughout; the glyph is flat, crisp and motionless.

Stage a small physical comedy entirely in the spacious left margin, clearly separated from the glyph. The lead is an original, enthusiastic boxy toy robot assembled from mismatched parts: a teal square torso, mustard hinged head, mismatched feet, one short arm and one conspicuously long accordion arm. Its only companion is a pink rubber pig with a broad round snout, tiny ears and a curly tail. Use expressive toy poses and simple glossy materials.

At the opening, the robot proudly attempts to pat the pig with its short arm, but its palm stops just out of reach. It looks from the short arm to its long arm with a delighted expression. Around 1.2 seconds, it extends the long arm and confidently pats downward, accidentally squashing the soft pig into a broad pink pancake; keep the snout and curly tail recognizable. Hold a brief anticipation beat as the robot peers down. At 2.4 seconds, the rubber pig rebounds to its round shape, flipping the robot’s loosely hinged long arm upward so that its own palm lands gently on its own head. The robot’s spring neck compresses, then slowly rises again beneath the resting palm. Let the robot blink in puzzled disbelief while the pig looks pleased. Use a soft rubber boing, never a loud impact. By 3.5 seconds, the robot figures it out: it takes one small step closer and successfully gives the pig a gentle pat with its short arm. The pig happily trots off to the left, and the robot follows, discreetly holding its unruly long arm against its torso. Both are fully outside the frame by 4.7 seconds.

From 4.7 through 8.0 seconds, hold completely still on the unobstructed centered 豬 alone for 3.3 full seconds. Maintain bright, soft studio lighting and strong stroke contrast, with no camera movement or flashing effects.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「豬、豬、小豬」. Pronounce the first 豬 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.5 seconds, and 小豬 around 5.4 seconds during the clean final hold, using ㄓㄨ consistently. Allow natural pauses and stop after 小豬. Keep toy sound effects quiet beneath the voice; use no music. The vocabulary is audio only. The single 豬 is the only visible writing: no subtitles, labels, other glyphs, logos or watermarks. All cast and objects are original stylized animated toys.
